title: Map
overview: Geography as a channel — never the only channel.
apply_when: Location, catchment, routes; a text alternative must exist.
not_when: A chart of non-geographic data, or a table of addresses with no map.

vs.why: the text alternative is often a table

role.overview: Geography as a channel — never the only channel.
role.apply_when: Location, catchment, routes; a text alternative must exist.
role.not_when: A chart of non-geographic data, or a table of addresses with no map.

size.overview: Highest in the size hierarchy — the easiest to hit.
size.apply_when: The view's main instance, or full-width on a small viewport.
size.not_when: A dense toolbar or a third option next to the main control.

size.apply_when: Ordinary use in forms, pages, and chrome.
size.not_when: The only control on a mobile screen that should span the width.

size.overview: Lowest in the size hierarchy — densest.
size.apply_when: Inline or chrome that sits beside content.
size.not_when: The page's primary instance, or a control under 44×44.

composition.overview: A list or table of the same places exists.
composition.apply_when: Any map used to choose or understand places.

state.overview: The map and its alternative are available.
state.not_when: A grey box with no list.
An empty map labeled as no results (empty_state).

accessibility.overview: The same places exist as text.
Zoom and pan controls have names.

keyboard.overview: Map controls and the alternative list are reachable.
If the map is a widget, arrows pan when that is the house — the list remains the alternative.
